questions.stem: The upward extension of thyroid swelling is prevented by which fascia which is attached to thyroid cartilage?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pretracheal Fascia
  • Pretracheal fascia prevents upward extension of thyroid swelling.

Pretracheal fascia:

  • It encloses and suspends the thyroid gland and forms its false capsule.
  • Attachments

Superiorly:

  1. Hyoid bone in the median plane
  2. oblique line of thyroid cartilage (laterally),
  3. Cricoid cartilage, (more laterally).

Inferiorly: Below the thyroid gland it encloses the inferior thyroid veins, passes behind the brachiocephalic veins, and finally blends with the arch of the aorta.

On either side: It fuses with the front of the carotid sheath deep to the sternocleidomastoid.

  • The posterior layer of the thyroid capsule is thick and forms a ligament of Berry.

Capsule of Thyroid gland




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 69, 70.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the type of joint in the given picture:
questions.solutionHtml:
Synovial joint

Image is showing costotransverse joint between rib and vertebrae

questions.stem: A patient presented with clinical features of ataxia and incoordination. What can be the site of lesion:
questions.solutionHtml:
Superior cerebellar artery

Given symptoms of patient signifies of cerebellar lesion

Three arteries supply blood to the cerebellum:-

  1. Superior cerebellar artery – branch of basilar artery
  2. Anterior inferior cerebellar artery - branch of basilar artery
  3. Posterior inferior cerebellar artery - branch of vertebral artery


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 209, 210.

questions.stem: The reason for the left long recurrent laryngeal nerve is due to the persistence of which arch artery?
questions.solutionHtml:
4th arch
  • Left recurrent laryngeal nerve winds around the arch of the aorta which derives from the 4th pharyngeal arch.
  • The recurrent laryngeal nerves branch off the vagus, the left at the aortic arch, and the right at the right subclavian artery.
  • The left RLN passes in front of the arch, and then wraps underneath and behind it.
  • The 4th pharyngeal arch artery on the right side gives rise to proximal part of right subclavian artery while on the left side it gives rise to the aortic arch.

Left recurrent laryngeal nerve




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 137.

questions.stem: A patient presented with the extension of the MCP joint and flexion of the IP joint. Which muscles are affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Interossei and lumbricals
  • Extension of MCP joint and flexion of IP joint - (This condition signifies of claw hand)
  • Interossei and lumbricals- flexes MCP (metacarpophalangeal) joints and extends IP (interphalangeal) joints.
  • Injury to Interossei and lumbricals leads to claw hand (extended MCP joint & flexed IP joint)


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No.216, 217.

questions.stem: Ligation of the common hepatic artery will impair blood supply in:

options.label: A
options.text: Right gastric and Right gastroepiploic artery

options.label: B
options.text: Right gastric and Left gastric artery

options.label: C
options.text: Right gastroepiploic and short gastric vessels

options.label: D
options.text: Right gastric and short gastric vessels

questions.answerText: Right gastric and Right gastroepiploic artery
questions.solutionHtml:
Right gastric and Right gastroepiploic artery
  • Right gastric artery arises from a common hepatic artery.
  • Right gastroepiploic artery- arises from gastroduodenal artery which is a branch of common hepatic artery.
  • SO LIGATION OF COMMON HEPATIC ARTERY will lead to impaired blood supply in Right gastric artery & Right gastroepiploic artery.

Arterial supply of Stomach

questions.stem: A patient presented with weakness of the right side of the face with the loss of pain and temperature sensation of the left side of the body. The lesion is most likely located at?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lateral pons
  • Lesion in pons leads to 7th nerve palsy as 7th nerve nucleus is present in Pons leading to Ipsilateral facial weakness along impairment of sensory part of 5th nerve (Present laterally in Pons) leading to Ipsilateral- loss of sensations on face.
  • As the pain and temp. sensation of the left side (Contralateral) is also affected s/o of lesion to the spinothalamic tract which runs laterally.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No. 350.

questions.stem: Tumor of the uncinate process of pancreas affects which of the following vessels?
questions.solutionHtml:
Superior mesenteric artery
  • Tumor of the uncinate process of pancreas leads to pressure on the superior mesenteric artery which passes above it. 

Arterial supply of Pancreas




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No. 125.

questions.stem: A man was brought to the emergency after meeting with an accident and injured his perineum. On examination-blood was seen at the tip of urethra. Swelling of penis and scrotum was noticed. He gets an urge to micturate but is unable to pass urine. This is because of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Bulbar urethra rupture

The bulbar urethra is susceptible to blunt force injuries because of its path along the perineum. Due to injury to bulbous spongy urethra (straddle injury or rupture of urethra below perineal membrane) urine can accumulate in:

  • Scrotum
  • Penis
  • Anterior abdominal wall
  • Superficial perineal pouch  

Urine accumulation in ruptured Bulbar urethra 




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No. 441.

questions.stemHtml: Illustration showing histology of cartilage. Identify the type of cartilage?
questions.solutionHtml:
Elastic cartilage

IMAGE given in the question is showing elastic cartilage.

Elastic cartilage, sometimes referred to as yellow fibrocartilage, is a type of cartilage that provides both strength and elasticity to certain parts of the body, such as the ears.

In elastic cartilage, chondrocytes are organised into elastic fibers, which make up a threadlike network or matrix.



Gray’s Anatomy, 42nd Edition, Page. No. 86, 87, 88.

questions.stem: Fertilization occurs in which part of the fallopian tube?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ampulla

FERTILIZATION occurs in AMPULLA of fallopian tube

Implantation of the zygote occurs in the uterus.

questions.stem: Remnants of Wolffian ducts in a female are located in which region?
questions.solutionHtml:
Broad ligament
  • GARTNER’S duct is a remnant of wolffian duct.
  • Remnants of the Wolffian duct (mesonephric duct) system in females may be retained within the layers of the Broad ligament between the uterus, fallopian tube, and ovary.

Gartner’s duct in broad ligament of uterus




Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No.270,272.

questions.stem: Episiotomy posteriorly beyond the perineal body injuring the structure immediately posterior to it. Which structure is injured?
questions.solutionHtml:
External anal sphincter
  • External anal sphincter is present just posterior to perineal body, therefore, external anal sphincter can be injured when episiotomy incision given posteriorly beyond perineal body.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No. 410.
